summary: This case study details a provider-simulation QA harness designed to replicate production timing and long-running AI generation bugs (90 to 600 seconds) in GenFlick Studio. It outlines strategies for structured stamps, fail-closed security gates, production-derived timing profiles, and observe floors to catch state-reclaiming and poll-backoff failures. The work provides practical, actionable insights for testing durable asynchronous operations.
strengths: Addresses a real-world, highly practical problem in testing long-running asynchronous AI generation jobs.
Well-documented timing profiles and explicit failure modes (fail-closed HTTP 403 on missing env gates).
Introduces clear observe floor logic to replace superficial single-snapshot test greens.
weaknesses: Relies on a private repository without public code or reproducible snippets outside of code excerpts.
Relies heavily on internal project-specific nomenclature and file paths that may be difficult for external readers to generalize.
suggestions: Provide a minimal open-source reference implementation or script structure for the simulation harness.
Include sample JSON output or logs demonstrating the failure strings returned by the observe floor helper.

claims.text: Long-running AI generation bugs live in the 90 to 600 second wait.
claims.source: General knowledge of video and image generation APIs (e.g., OpenAI, Fal, Remotion) where generation times frequently span minutes.
